case_name: Dajya Moshya Bhil and Others v State of Maharashtra
respondent:
State of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

3 August 1984
Cr.A. No. 361 of 1984. (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 16 November 1983 of the Bombay High Court in Cr.A. No. 1040 of 1981).
The Order of the Court was as follows :
1.  Special leave granted limited to the question whether appellants 2 and 3 shared the common intention with appellant 1 for committing murder of Gunjarya son of Dhanya.
2.  It may at once be mentioned that the special leave petition on behalf of petitioner 1 was dismissed at the admission stage.

facts: At a festival described as 'Indal' an altercation took place between deceased Gunjarya on one hand and appellants 2 and 3 on the other on account of the profane language used by appellants 2 and 3 who were then inebriated.

Both of them were slapped by Gunjarya. The dispute consequent upon this altercation was settled by the local panchayat in which both appellants 2 and 3 on one hand and deceased Gunjarya on the other, were fined Rs 5 each.

On May 26, 1981 when deceased Gunjarya accompanied by his two brothers Gobji and Pandys in company of PW 3 Hajarya, PW 4 Dajya and PW 5 Jahangriya and two others were busy dismantling the hut of one Bamanya for the purpose of erecting a new hut on the nearby plot, the three accused came together and declared their intention of avenging the insult inflicted on them by Gunjarya at the time of 'Indal' festival.

At that time accused 1 was armed with a Dharya while appellants 2 and 3 were unarmed. Immediately all the three of them rushed towards deceased Gunjarya and when Gunjarya tried to escape he was chased.
issues: Whether appellants 2 and 3 shared the common intention with appellant 1 for committing murder of Gunjarya
petitioner_arguments: Appellants 2 and 3 though they were in the company of the appellant 1 were shown to be unarmed. The High Court has overlooked this most important circumstance.
It is not suggested that the appellants are interrelated. Therefore, it is not shown that appellant 1 was in any manner involved in this quarrel.
respondent_arguments: The three circumstances relied upon by Mr Bhasme in support of his submission are : (i) that the three accused came together; (ii) that all the three accused had a common motive to avenge the incident that occurred at 'Indal' festival; and (iii) that when the victim of assault Gunjarya tried to escape all the three of them chased Gunjarya.
court_reasoning: Standing by itself this circumstance may be sufficient to suggest that three had some common intention. The question is whether they had common intention to commit murder of Gunjarya.
It would be contrary to common sense to hold that appellants 2 and 3 accompanied appellant 1 with the avowed object of committing murder of Gunjarya yet came unarmed.

The High Court has recorded a finding that at the time of the festival in the house of Parsi Basara, a quarrel took place between Gunjarya on one hand and appellants 2 and 3 on the other. There is not the slightest reference to the presence or participation of appellant 1, who is shown to be the principal culprit of the offence, in that quarrel.
holding: The conviction of appellants 2 and 3 for an offence u/s. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code cannot to sustained.
Appellants 2 and 3 are shown to have committed an offence u/s. 326 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and they should be convicted accordingly.
